title: Mental health as a social issue
subtitle: The silent epidemic
subject: comprendreLeMonde
description: Mental health represents **20% of illnesses in the world**, but only receives 2% of health budgets. Here is why this long-forgotten cause is becoming a major social issue.

hero.hook: One in five illnesses in the world affects the mind, but receives barely 2% of health budgets.

blocks.text: Long neglected by medicine, mental health is becoming one of the great challenges of the 21st century. It is not limited to the absence of psychiatric disorders: it is a state of well-being which allows everyone to realize their potential and to face the difficulties of life.
However, a striking paradox persists: these disorders represent around 20% of diseases worldwide, but receive only 2% of health budgets. This course explores the roots of this silent crisis.

**depression** is today the leading global cause of disability, ahead of heart disease and diabetes. This disease, marked by lasting sadness and a loss of interest in everything, affects all categories of the population, but remains underdiagnosed in many regions of the world.

blocks.caption: Depression is today the leading global cause of disability.

blocks.text: Generalized anxiety affects approximately 300 million people worldwide. This suffering sometimes leads to suicide, responsible for 700,000 deaths per year, a figure greater than the number of victims of wars and natural disasters combined.
The word “melancholy” comes from ancient Greek and literally means “black bile”. In ancient times, depression was thought to be caused by an excess of this fluid in the body.

In 2019, the World Health Organization took a symbolic step in recognizing  as a work-related phenomenon. This recognition shifts responsibility from the individual alone to their work environment. [[Burn-out (professional exhaustion)]]

While the entire population is affected, adolescents and young adults are of particular concern. In the United States, anxiety and depression among 12-25 year olds have almost doubled in a decade, with a clear turning point around 2012.

blocks.caption: The explosion of social media coincides with a marked increase in anxiety among young people.

blocks.text: This date corresponds to the generalization of the smartphone and social networks. Psychologist Jean Twenge believes that this change has disrupted the sociability of young people: the , where we compare ourselves to unrealistic standards of life, creates a deep feeling of inadequacy. [[Upward social comparison]]

Added to this are  and lack of sleep caused by the light from screens. Social networks operate on  loops which can become addictive and distract young people from sport or restful sleep. [[Cyber-victimization]] [[Dopaminergic enhancement]]

Mental health is not just about privacy: it also directly affects productivity. The annual cost of burnout and suffering at work is estimated at $300 billion per year in the United States alone, between absences, repeated departures and employees present but unable to work effectively.

blocks.caption: The cost of burnout is hundreds of billions of dollars each year.

blocks.text: Faced with this cost, companies are developing prevention programs, but the challenge remains in poor countries, where consulting a psychiatrist is almost impossible. One of the most powerful levers remains destigmatization: when a public figure like athlete Simone Biles speaks openly about her difficulties, she helps transform a source of shame into a real health issue.

The future of mental health depends on our ability to move from medicine that treats the crisis once it arrives, to a preventative approach. This requires rethinking town planning, schooling and the pace of work to reduce sources of stress before they have an impact.
New avenues are emerging, such as digital therapies or artificial intelligence, to compensate for the lack of practitioners, although these tools also raise questions about data confidentiality.

Mental health is also linked to current major crises: the concept of eco-anxiety clearly shows how global threats, such as the climate, directly affect our psychological balance. Recognizing mental health as an essential pillar of our societies becomes a condition for confronting future crises.

Mental health represents 20% of illnesses worldwide but only 2% of health budgets. Between depression, burn-out and the impact of digital technology on young people, it is becoming a societal issue as urgent as it is economic.
